results.content:
And ElvixAI gets its own section:

“ElvixAI is an AI backlink outreach agent that finds relevant websites, discovers contacts, writes personalized outreach and follows up automatically.”

If my goal is just traditional SEO authority, the first link might look stronger on paper.

But if my goal is to make ElvixAI associated with:

AI backlink tools

backlink outreach software

AI link building

automated backlink outreach

I'd choose the second placement every time.

Because the context is much stronger.

This is the big change with GEO

Traditional link building has mostly been about transferring authority from one website to another.

GEO adds another layer.

Now I also care about what the page says about my brand.

I care about the other companies mentioned next to me. [...] Do they mention my competitors?

Is my brand missing?

Does my product genuinely belong there?

Is the article still being updated?

Can I contact the author or editor?

You can also do the same thing inside ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini.

Ask:

“What are the best tools for X?”

Then look at the brands and sources that keep appearing.

If certain websites repeatedly influence recommendations in your space, those are probably websites worth paying attention to.

This is also how I'm thinking about ElvixAI

This problem is actually one of the reasons I've been building ElvixAI the way I have.

I don't want it to just find websites with a decent DR and start emailing them.

That's not enough.

The better system is:

Find pages where your product actually belongs. [...] 🚨 3. Context around the mention

This part is massively underrated.

A backlink like this:

“You can also use ElvixAI.”

isn't nearly as strong contextually as:

“ElvixAI is an AI backlink outreach tool that automates prospecting, contact discovery, personalized emails and follow-ups.”

The second mention clearly tells a reader (and potentially an AI system consuming that page) what the product is.

Your brand becomes associated with a category and a use case.

That's what I want.

🚨 4. Competitor presence

This is one of my favorite signals.

If a page already mentions 3 of my competitors but doesn't mention me

that's probably a page I want to be on.

For example, if an article says:

“Best AI SEO tools: Semrush, Ahrefs, Surfer...”

results.title: How broken links affect SEO: A complete guide
results.content:
Ready to see how your site is doing? Start by getting a quick snapshot of your website's health. Run a free scan with the eesel AI Broken Link Checker and find out where you stand in just a few minutes.

## Frequently Asked Questions

How do broken links affect SEO in terms of user experience?

They create a frustrating experience. When users hit a "404 Not Found" page, they often leave your site immediately, which increases your bounce rate. Search engines can interpret this as a sign that your site isn't helpful, potentially leading to lower rankings over time.
